themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints in Central Harlem spiked to 8 complaints THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week—a 1,180% increase (z-score: 6.64)—suggesting a sudden change in park activity or enforcement gaps that warrants investigation into which parks are affected and why.
evidence: 8 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.64)
Timing coincides with warming weather; unclear if event-driven or operational change
reporting_angles: Which Central Harlem parks are generating complaints? Are new events, vendor activities, or enforcement gaps driving the spike?
Interview Parks Department and local residents to identify specific locations and activities causing noise

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints jumped to 3 reports LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a rapid increase in unauthorized signage that could indicate campaign activity, unauthorized advertising, or declining enforcement.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
2,300% increase represents one of the highest statistical deviations in the dataset
No corroborating community board or news mentions; nature of postings unknown
reporting_angles: Visual survey: Document what illegal postings exist across the district—political, commercial, or other categories
Contact NYPD and Sanitation Department to understand why enforcement may be lagging and what triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Request Surge
themes_detail.summary: Requests for litter baskets surged to 5 complaints THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 1,233% increase (z-score: 9.55)—indicating residents are perceiving or experiencing a sudden shortage of street sanitation infrastructure.
evidence: 5 litter basket requests THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.55)
1,233% spike is statistically significant and among highest deviations in dataset
Coincides with warmer weather and likely increased outdoor activity; may reflect seasonal or operational gaps
reporting_angles: Are specific neighborhoods or commercial corridors reporting shortages? Map the complaints to identify service gaps.
Interview Sanitation Department: Have baskets been removed, relocated, or is maintenance lagging in Central Harlem?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints increased to 6 reports LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.6 per week—an 860% spike (z-score: 4.84)—suggesting a potential increase in vandalism or a decline in cleanup responsiveness.
evidence: 6 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.84)
860% increase indicates significant anomaly but with small absolute volume
No community board or news mentions; unclear if driven by new vandalism or backlog in removals
reporting_angles: Are graffiti complaints concentrated in specific areas (commercial strips, transit stations, residential blocks)?
Assess Department of Sanitation response times: Is the spike driven by more vandalism or slower cleanup?

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Decline
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints DROPPED 35% THIS WEEK to 169 reports from a baseline of 260.1 per week (z-score: -5.12)—an anomalous decrease that merits investigation into whether building closures, enforcement, or data gaps explain the sudden shift.
evidence: 169 residential noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 260.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (35% decline, z-score: -5.12)
Statistically significant negative deviation suggests change in reporting, conditions, or enforcement
Counterintuitive given warming weather typically increases outdoor noise; may indicate data anomaly or enforcement shift
reporting_angles: Verify with 311 system: Is the decline a data issue (system downtime, reporting lag) or a real change?
Interview NYPD and community residents: Has increased enforcement or changed conditions reduced noise complaints?
